newsitem.title: USA: Dow tops 6,000 but ends lower; Nasdaq sets record.
newsitem.headline: Dow tops 6,000 but ends lower; Nasdaq sets record.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average topped 6,000 points for the first time Monday before ending lower on profit-taking, but the Nasdaq index scored its first record close in four months as technology stocks rallied.
The 30-stock Dow index was off 13.05 points at 5,979.81 following a brief run-up to 6,002.17. The Nasdaq Composite rose 3.31 to 1,250.87, beating its June 5 record finish of 1,249.15.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,208 to 1,123 on moderate volume of 380 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said the Dow was due for a pause after setting its 27th record close for the year Friday at 5,992.86 as a weaker-than-expected report on September jobs lessened Wall Street's fears that the Federal Reserve would need to raise interest rates to slow the economy's growth.

"We're recovering from a little nosebleed after Friday's highs and some people are taking profits off the table," said Ken Ducey, head of trading at BT Brokerage. "People seem fairly convinced sometime this week we'll close above 6,000."

Other stock market gauges also set new milestones, with the Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks gaining 1.91 points to 703.37, its fifth record close in the past six trading sessions. The NYSE Composite index was at a new high, up 0.58 to 374.74.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- also set a new high at 6,897.392 up 11.801 or 0.17 percent.
The Dow's rise through the 6,000 level came just days before the market marks the sixth anniversary this Friday of its current bull run.
The moonshot-like jump in the Dow started on Oct. 11, 1990, with the index climbing from 2,365 and the S&P 500 index from 295.
William LeFevre, senior analyst at Ehrenkrantz King Nussbaum was unfazed by the 6,000 milestone and upcoming anniversary.
"It's a bull market. Relax and enjoy it," he said.

As for Monday's trading, Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter, said, "A couple of the Dow stocks got hurt but oils are very strong and some tech stocks are doing well. The market is consolidating after a big move Friday."

The bulk of the Dow's losses came from Eastman Kodak, which fell 3-1/4 to 75-3/8. Kodak Chairman George Fisher said the company may be embroiled in a dispute over opening the Japanese film market for 18 more months.

Oil stocks were bolstered by news of a planned merger of the U.S. refining and marketing operations of three of the world's largest oil companies -- Texaco, Royal/Dutch Shell Group and Star Enterprise, a joint venture between Texaco and state oil company of Saudi Arabia, Saudi Aramco.
Texaco rose 1-1/8 to 96-3/4, and Chevron rose 7/8 to 65-3/8.
Technology stocks were buoyed by speculation that the group would report upbeat earnings for the latest quarter.

Among the winners, Intel rose 2-15/16 to 104-5/8, Microsoft was up 1-1/8 to 137-1/2, International Business Machines added 1 to 127-7/8, Hewlett-Packard was up 2 to 45-5/8 and Motorola was up 1 to 49-1/4.
Cheyenne Software climbed 7-5/8 to 30 after Computer Associates, which gained 2-1/8 to 64-1/2, agreed to buy Cheyenne for $1.2 billion in cash.
Thomas & Betts lost 1-7/8 to 37-7/8 and Augat climbed 4-3/8 to 25-1/4 after Thomas & Betts agreed to buy the maker of circuit connection products in a stock exchange deal valued at $550 million.
Westell Technologies tumbled 12-3/8 to 34. France's Alcatel Telecom won a contract to supply modem technology to four regional Bell companies, a contract some had expected Westell to win.
Earthgrains surged 6 to 45 on unexpectedly strong earnings.
HFS Inc. rose 3-3/4 to 78-3/8 on news that it agreed to buy Resorts Condominium Inc. for $625 million.
Raytheon continued to fall, losing 2-5/8 to 46-1/4 after Friday's earnings warning. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.33 to 582.22. The average NYSE share was up 7 cents.
